title: AF-4-part-1
description: Airframe exam covering landing gear systems: shock struts, retraction/extension, brakes and brake systems, steering, tires and wheels, and related components and inspection practices, drawn from the AF-4 landing gear question/answer bank.

questions.question: Which hydraulic configuration on light aircraft is easy to service?
options: A. A fully centralized multi-system network
questions.explanation: A self-contained power pack bundles the pump, reservoir, and valves into one compact unit, making it simpler to service on light aircraft.

questions.question: What should be installed when removing the landing gear?
options: B. A chock on the nose wheel only
questions.explanation: Before removing or working on the landing gear, a down-lock/ground safety pin is installed to mechanically prevent accidental retraction.

questions.question: What does an isolated (independent) hydraulic brake system have?
options: A. Independent brakes, separate from the main aircraft hydraulic system
B. Shared pressure with flight controls only
questions.explanation: An isolated/independent brake system has its own self-contained hydraulic supply (reservoir, master cylinders) separate from the main aircraft hydraulic system.

questions.question: What does "positive locking" refer to with respect to landing gear?
options: C. A ground landing gear lock (mechanical down-lock device)
questions.explanation: Positive locking refers to a mechanical ground lock that physically secures the landing gear in the down position, independent of hydraulic pressure.

questions.question: Which type of landing gear absorbs landing energy primarily through a flexing metal element?
questions.explanation: Spring-type gear (such as a tapered spring steel or composite leg) absorbs and dissipates landing shock through the flexing of the spring material itself.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a tire chine?
options: A. To deflect water sideways, away from the engine/airframe
B. To increase tire traction on dry runways
questions.explanation: Chine tires have a molded deflector rib that throws water and slush sideways during takeoff/landing, helping protect aft-mounted engines from spray ingestion.

questions.question: Which landing gear arrangement has the two main gear positioned forward of the aircraft's center of gravity?
questions.explanation: In conventional (tailwheel) gear arrangements, the main wheels sit forward of the CG, with a small tailwheel supporting the rear of the aircraft.

questions.question: Overinflated aircraft tires may cause what type of damage?
options: A. Excessive wear on the shoulders of the tread
C. Excessive wear in the center of the tread
questions.explanation: An overinflated tire bulges in the center of its contact patch, concentrating wear and causing premature tread wear specifically down the center.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a trunnion?
options: A. A hydraulic valve that controls gear sequencing
B. A tire bead seating ring
C. A fixed structural extension with bearing surfaces that allows the entire landing gear assembly to pivot/move
questions.explanation: The trunnion is a structural pivot point, fixed to the aircraft, with bearings that let the landing gear leg rotate for retraction/extension.

questions.question: A power-boost brake system is typically used on aircraft that are...
options: A. Too slow and too light to need hydraulic brakes at all
B. Only used on ultralight gliders
C. Too fast and too heavy for simple master-cylinder-only brakes (yet not large enough for a full power brake system)
questions.explanation: Power-boost brakes add hydraulic assistance to pilot-applied pedal force for aircraft whose speed/weight exceeds what simple mechanical/hydraulic master cylinders alone can handle.

questions.question: Why does a metering pin in an oleo strut have a tapered shape?
options: A. To reduce the weight of the pin
B. To gradually increase resistance to fluid flow as the strut compresses
C. To allow easier manufacturing only
questions.explanation: The tapered metering pin varies the size of the orifice it passes through as the strut compresses, progressively increasing flow resistance (and damping) through the stroke.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the torque link (torque arm/scissor link) on a landing gear strut?
options: A. To align the wheel (keep the lower sliding cylinder from rotating relative to the upper cylinder)
B. To absorb all vertical landing shock
C. To steer the nose wheel electrically
questions.explanation: Torque links connect the upper and lower strut cylinders, preventing the lower (axle) cylinder from rotating out of alignment while still allowing the strut to extend/compress.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a landing gear safety device?
questions.explanation: A towing lug is a structural attachment point for ground handling, not a safety device meant to prevent inadvertent gear retraction or indicate gear status.

questions.question: What is the purpose of shimmy dampers on landing gear?
options: A. To absorb vertical landing impact
B. To steer the nose wheel
C. To reduce wheel vibration (shimmy) at high speed
questions.explanation: Shimmy dampers resist the rapid side-to-side oscillation (shimmy) that can occur in a free-castering wheel at higher taxi/rollout speeds.

questions.question: Differential braking is used as an additional form of directional control when...
options: A. The normal nose wheel steering system has failed
C. The flaps are fully extended
questions.explanation: If nose wheel steering fails, applying brakes differentially (more on one main wheel than the other) can help the pilot maintain or change direction during taxi/rollout.

questions.question: Which valve relieves tire and wheel pressure if the tire/wheel assembly is exposed to overinflation or overheating?
questions.explanation: A thermal/pressure relief plug melts or vents at a set pressure/temperature, safely deflating an overinflated or overheated tire before it can burst violently.

questions.question: What keeps the hydraulic pressure of the brakes and steering systems maintained separately in some designs?
options: A. A single shared reservoir with no separation
C. An accumulator and compensator arrangement
questions.explanation: Dedicated accumulators and compensator valves allow brake and steering hydraulic pressures to be independently maintained without interfering with each other.

questions.question: During tire inspection, if the measured result falls within the operational range shown on the service chart, what should be done?
options: A. Replace the tire immediately regardless of chart result
B. Deflate the tire to zero pressure
questions.explanation: If wear or damage measurements fall within acceptable limits per the service chart, the tire remains airworthy and operation continues normally.

questions.question: The pilot has full (differential) control of the brakes for taxiing and towing when...
options: B. Wheel speed is less than about 20 mph
C. The parking brake is set
questions.explanation: At low taxi/towing speeds (roughly under 20 mph), differential and full brake authority is typically available to the pilot for maneuvering.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of using carbon brake/wheel assemblies?
options: A. Their excessive weight compared with steel brakes
questions.explanation: Carbon brakes, while lighter and more heat-tolerant than steel, are considerably more expensive to manufacture.

questions.question: How do non-shock-absorbing (rigid) landing gear designs dissipate impact energy?
options: A. By venting energy through hydraulic fluid heating
B. By transferring impact energy into the overall airframe structure over time, rather than at a single instant
C. By compressing an internal spring
questions.explanation: Rigid (non-absorbing) gear relies on the overall airframe's flexibility to spread out and absorb impact energy over the structure, rather than a dedicated shock-absorbing strut.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the compensator (compensating) port in a brake master cylinder?
options: B. To provide emergency brake pressure
C. To allow fluid to move between the reservoir and master cylinder as fluid volume changes with temperature
questions.explanation: The compensator port lets fluid expand into or contract from the reservoir as temperature changes, preventing pressure buildup in the brake line when the brakes are released.

questions.question: What stabilizes the landing gear longitudinally (fore and aft)?
questions.explanation: The drag strut (or drag brace) resists fore-and-aft loads on the landing gear leg, providing longitudinal stability, while side struts handle lateral loads.

questions.question: What is used to regulate the flow of hydraulic fluid as the landing gear strut is compressed?
questions.explanation: The metering pin, moving through a variable orifice as the strut compresses, regulates oil flow and controls the shock strut's damping characteristics.

questions.question: What is used to reduce brake system pressure while increasing fluid volume delivered to the brakes?
questions.explanation: A brake debooster reduces high system pressure to a lower, safer brake pressure while delivering a larger volume of fluid, matching brake piston requirements.

questions.question: Where are the brakes of a landing gear typically mounted?
options: A. On the wheel (on a flange associated with the wheel/axle assembly)
questions.explanation: Brake assemblies are mounted on or around the wheel, commonly attached to a flange on the axle/torque plate associated with the wheel assembly.

questions.question: What is checked during inspection of control cables?
options: A. Only the cable color coding
B. Only the cable's manufacturing date stamp
questions.explanation: Cable inspections check for proper tension (safetying) and tightness of connections, along with wear, corrosion, and broken strands.

questions.question: A "spongy" (soft, mushy) brake pedal feel typically indicates what?
options: C. Air trapped in the hydraulic brake system
questions.explanation: Air trapped in the brake hydraulic lines compresses under pedal pressure, producing a soft, spongy pedal feel instead of firm, immediate braking response.

questions.question: What does the compensator port do in an independent master cylinder brake system?
options: A. Permits fluid to flow toward or away from the reservoir as fluid volume changes with temperature
B. Boosts brake pressure using engine power
C. Locks the brakes when parked
questions.explanation: The compensator port equalizes fluid volume between the master cylinder and reservoir as temperature-driven expansion or contraction occurs, preventing residual pressure.

questions.question: Other than the steering tiller, what other cockpit control is used to steer the nose gear?
questions.explanation: On many aircraft, rudder pedal inputs are mechanically or hydraulically linked to provide limited nose wheel steering, in addition to a dedicated tiller for tighter ground maneuvering.

questions.question: Multiple-disc brakes are typically used in conjunction with what type of system?
options: A. A simple mechanical cable brake system
B. No hydraulic system at all
C. A power-boost master cylinder brake system
questions.explanation: Multiple-disc brake assemblies, which handle higher loads, are commonly paired with power-boost (hydraulically assisted) master cylinder systems.

questions.question: If the piston return spring malfunctions in a brake master cylinder, what happens?
options: A. The brakes will apply with double force
B. The reservoir will overfill immediately
C. The piston will not retract fully back to its released position
questions.explanation: A failed return spring prevents the master cylinder piston from fully returning after brake release, which can cause dragging brakes or incomplete fluid return.

questions.question: During brake inspection and repair, what is a correct consideration regarding mismatched components?
options: A. Any lining material can be used regardless of thickness
B. Brake linings never need inspection
C. Brake lining material/thickness must match the approved specification for that brake assembly
questions.explanation: Using a mismatched or incorrect brake lining (wrong thickness/material) compared with the approved specification can lead to improper brake performance or premature failure.

questions.question: What is the most common bleeding method used for a power brake system?
options: A. Bleeding from bottom to top
B. Bleeding from top to bottom
C. No bleeding is ever required
questions.explanation: Power brake systems are commonly bled starting from the top (master cylinder/reservoir end) working down toward the brake unit to purge trapped air effectively.

questions.question: What is true when removing an aircraft wheel and brake assembly?
options: A. The shimmy damper must always be removed first
B. The brake hose assembly must be disconnected
C. The tire must be fully inflated during removal
questions.explanation: Removing a wheel and brake assembly requires disconnecting the brake hose (fluid line) from the brake unit before the wheel can be taken off the axle.

questions.question: What is a means of reducing parasite drag related to the landing gear?
questions.explanation: Retracting the landing gear into the airframe during flight removes it from the airstream, significantly reducing parasite drag compared with fixed gear.

questions.question: The steering tiller is used to steer the aircraft from where?
options: A. The ground crew's tow vehicle only
questions.explanation: The tiller is a cockpit control, typically on the side console, used by the pilot to steer the nose wheel during ground operations, especially tight turns.

questions.question: What device locks the landing gear control lever whenever the aircraft is on the ground?
options: C. A landing gear safety (squat) switch
questions.explanation: The squat (weight-on-wheels) switch senses ground contact and mechanically/electrically locks out the gear control lever to prevent inadvertent retraction on the ground.

questions.question: What returns the brake pressure plate to its released position when the brake is released?
questions.explanation: A return spring pulls the brake pressure plate/piston back when hydraulic pressure is removed, releasing the brake and restoring clearance.

questions.question: The brake and steering systems are typically mounted, respectively, on which wheel assemblies?
options: A. The nose wheel (brakes) and main wheels (steering)
B. The main wheels (brakes) and the auxiliary/nose wheel (steering)
C. Both systems share the same single wheel
questions.explanation: Brakes are mounted on the main landing gear wheels, while steering is applied through the nose (auxiliary) landing gear.

questions.question: What is true when removing an aircraft tire?
options: A. The brake hose must always be cut
B. The shimmy damper should be disconnected (if applicable to that gear leg)
C. The axle nut should never be loosened
questions.explanation: Depending on the gear design, the shimmy damper linkage may need to be disconnected to allow removal of the wheel/tire assembly from the strut.

questions.question: What describes a brake system that has its own dedicated hydraulic fluid supply?
options: A. A power brake actuating system using the main aircraft hydraulics
questions.explanation: An independent brake system carries its own self-contained fluid reservoir, separate from the main aircraft hydraulic system that powers other functions.

questions.question: During taxiing with a spring-oleo type shock strut, shock/vibration is dampened primarily by what?
questions.explanation: In a spring-oleo design, the mechanical spring element provides the primary damping/absorption of shocks and vibration during ground operations.

questions.question: Which component keeps the steering system under continuous pressure for shimmy damping?
questions.explanation: A compensator unit maintains a steady preload/pressure in the steering/shimmy damper circuit, ensuring continuous damping action.

questions.question: The plies in radial tires are laid at approximately what angle to the direction of tire rotation?
questions.explanation: Radial tire construction lays the cord plies at approximately 90 degrees to the direction of rotation (radially across the tire), distinguishing it from bias-ply construction.

questions.question: How are landing gear positions (up/down) typically sensed for cockpit indication?
questions.explanation: Proximity switches sense the physical position of the gear (extended/retracted) and feed signals to the cockpit indicating system.

questions.question: What is the name of the hydraulically operated valve that prevents the landing gear actuator from lowering the main gear before the wheel well doors are open?
questions.explanation: A priority/sequence valve ensures the gear doors open first before allowing gear extension, maintaining the correct order of operations.

questions.question: What does pulling a manual landing gear extension handle do?
options: B. Releases the gear's mechanical uplock, allowing it to free-fall and lock down
questions.explanation: The manual extension handle mechanically releases the uplock so gravity (and sometimes airflow) can lower and lock the gear in an emergency, independent of hydraulics.

questions.question: Which component is regarded as the "brain" of the antiskid braking system?
questions.explanation: The antiskid control unit processes wheel speed sensor data and commands brake pressure modulation to prevent skidding, acting as the system's central controller.

questions.question: In which type of wheel construction is an O-ring used between the wheel halves?
questions.explanation: Split-type wheels bolt two halves together around the tire bead, and an O-ring seal between the halves maintains an airtight seal.

questions.question: On which half of a split-type wheel are the brakes typically fitted?
questions.explanation: Brake components are mounted on the inboard half of a split wheel, facing the aircraft centerline where the brake mechanism attaches to the axle/torque plate.

questions.question: What is the role of the sequence valve in a landing gear system?
options: A. To ensure proper operation of the landing gear and doors in the correct order
questions.explanation: A sequence valve times hydraulic flow so that, for example, gear doors open before the gear itself moves, ensuring correct mechanical sequencing.

questions.question: What is an advantage of conventional (tailwheel) landing gear?
options: A. Easier ground visibility over the nose
B. Better suitability for rough, unimproved surface operation
questions.explanation: Conventional gear's design, with larger main wheels well forward and a small tailwheel, tends to handle rough or soft unimproved surfaces better than tricycle gear.

questions.question: During brake inspection and repair, which of the following describes a correct maintenance consideration (as opposed to a mismatch)?
options: A. Linings never wear and never need inspection
B. Lining wear should be checked against specified limits before continued use
C. Any lining thickness is acceptable regardless of specification
questions.explanation: Routine brake inspection includes checking lining wear against the manufacturer's specified limits to determine if replacement is needed.

questions.question: Which type of brake design uses a drum with an internal expanding tube?
questions.explanation: Expander-tube brakes use a flexible tube inside a drum that expands under hydraulic pressure, pressing brake blocks against the drum to create braking force.

questions.question: Which type of landing gear design dissipates landing energy primarily into the atmosphere (as heat)?
options: C. The oleo-pneumatic (air/oil) shock strut type
questions.explanation: Oleo-pneumatic struts force hydraulic fluid through a metering orifice, converting kinetic landing energy into heat that dissipates into the surrounding air.

questions.question: What landing gear device is used for water surface operations?
questions.explanation: Floats (pontoons) replace or supplement conventional landing gear to allow an aircraft to operate from water surfaces.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to lubricate wheel bearings immediately after cleaning and inspection?
options: A. To add weight for balance
B. To prevent corrosion of the freshly cleaned bearing surfaces
C. To change the bearing's color for inspection
questions.explanation: Freshly cleaned bearings are stripped of protective lubricant and are vulnerable to rapid corrosion if not promptly relubricated.

questions.question: Which component aligns the nose gear (centers it) before it retracts into the wheel well?
questions.explanation: A centering cam mechanically straightens (centers) the nose wheel as the strut extends, ensuring it fits properly into the wheel well upon retraction.

questions.question: What is the function of the metering pin in an oleo shock strut?
options: A. To control the flow of hydraulic fluid as the strut is compressed
B. To lock the gear in the extended position
questions.explanation: The metering pin passes through the orifice as the strut compresses, progressively restricting oil flow and controlling the damping force throughout the stroke.

questions.question: What is the name of the part at the lower end of the strut (lower cylinder) that provides for installation of the aircraft wheel?
questions.explanation: The axle is the stub shaft at the bottom of the landing gear leg onto which the wheel and tire assembly is mounted.

questions.question: Why are large airplanes often equipped with carbon disc brakes?
options: A. Because carbon brakes offer light weight and extended service life compared with steel brakes
B. Because carbon brakes are cheaper to manufacture than steel brakes
C. Because carbon brakes require no maintenance at all
questions.explanation: Carbon brakes are favored on large aircraft because they are lighter and last longer (higher heat capacity, slower wear) than equivalent steel brake stacks.

questions.question: Which component is attached to the aircraft structure and allows the landing gear to pivot?
questions.explanation: The trunnion is the fixed pivot attachment point on the aircraft structure around which the landing gear leg rotates during retraction and extension.

questions.question: Which part of a tire is subject to wear from contact with the runway?
questions.explanation: The tread is the outer rubber surface designed to contact the runway, and it is the part that wears down with use.

questions.question: What part of a tire provides the anchor point that seats the tire onto the wheel rim?
questions.explanation: The bead is the reinforced edge of the tire that seats against the wheel rim, anchoring the tire securely and maintaining an airtight seal.

questions.question: Which valve is mechanically operated to control the landing gear and its doors in the correct sequence?
questions.explanation: A mechanically actuated sequence valve ensures gear and door movements occur in the proper order during retraction/extension.

questions.question: What is an example of a brake master cylinder design that uses an external (remote) reservoir?
options: A. A fully integral master cylinder with no reservoir
B. The Goodyear-type master cylinder (with remote reservoir)
C. A power-boost-only design with no master cylinder
questions.explanation: Some master cylinder designs, such as certain Goodyear units, use a separate external reservoir connected by a line rather than an integral built-in reservoir.

questions.question: For light aircraft, how does the pilot typically operate landing gear retraction and extension?
options: A. Only through a fully automatic computer system
questions.explanation: Many light aircraft use a simple mechanical or hydraulic system operated by the pilot moving a gear lever manually, rather than a complex automated system.

questions.question: What are systems called that use the aircraft's main hydraulic system as the power source to apply the brakes?
questions.explanation: Power brake systems tap into the aircraft's main hydraulic system pressure (rather than a dedicated independent reservoir) to actuate the brakes.

questions.question: When differential brakes are applied, which landing gear is used to steer the aircraft?
questions.explanation: Differential braking applies more braking force to one main gear wheel than the other, creating a turning moment to help steer the aircraft.

questions.question: If the landing gear wheels converge toward each other at the front when viewed from above (along the longitudinal axis), this condition is called what?
questions.explanation: Toe-in describes wheels angled so their leading edges point slightly inward toward each other, as opposed to toe-out where they point outward.

questions.question: Which type of tire has an inner liner (built into the tire itself rather than using a separate tube)?
questions.explanation: Tubeless tires incorporate an air-impermeable inner liner molded into the tire, eliminating the need for a separate inner tube.

questions.question: Which tire tread design is the most common on aircraft?
questions.explanation: Rib tread, with continuous circumferential grooves, is the most common aircraft tire tread pattern, providing good directional stability and wet traction.

questions.question: Overinflated aircraft tires may cause what condition?
questions.explanation: Overinflation causes the tire to bulge, concentrating contact pressure (and therefore wear) in the center of the tread, leading to premature wear there.

questions.question: During approach for landing, hydraulic pressure is initially fed to what component?
options: A. The landing gear door actuator
questions.explanation: Gear extension sequencing typically opens the gear doors first by feeding pressure to the door actuator before the gear leg itself is lowered.

questions.question: How is the landing gear down-and-locked position typically indicated in the cockpit?
questions.explanation: Standard cockpit indication uses a green light (per gear) to show that the landing gear is fully extended and mechanically locked down.

questions.question: Which type of brake system is typically used on medium-sized airplanes?
options: A. A simple mechanical cable brake system only
B. A full independent power brake system identical to large transports
questions.explanation: Medium-sized aircraft commonly use power-boost brake systems, which add hydraulic assistance to pedal input without the full complexity of large transport power brake systems.
